Section A: answer ALL the questions (15 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: answer ALL four questions; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.

(i) Given the function $f(x)=5+4x-x^{2}$.

(ii) A function $f$ is defined on $\mathbb{R}$, the set of real numbers, by $f(x)=x^{3}+2x^{2}+ax+b$. When $f(x)$ is divided by $(x+1)$, the remainder is $0$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) Construct a table of values of $y$ against $x$ for $-2\leq x\leq 6$.
(i)(b) Taking 2 cm to represent 1 unit on the $x$-axis and 1 cm to represent 1 unit on the $y$-axis, draw the graph of $y=f(x)$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Axes:** $x$-axis from $-2$ to $6$ (16 cm long, 2 cm per unit); $y$-axis from $-7$ to $9$ (16 cm long, 1 cm per unit).

**Points to plot:** $(-2,-7)$, $(-1,0)$, $(0,5)$, $(1,8)$, $(2,9)$, $(3,8)$, $(4,5)$, $(5,0)$, $(6,-7)$.

Join the points with a **smooth curve**. It is an inverted U-shape (a parabola opening downwards) with its maximum point (turning point) at $(2, 9)$ and axis of symmetry $x=2$. It cuts the $x$-axis at $(-1,0)$ and $(5,0)$ and the $y$-axis at $(0,5)$. Label the axes and the curve $y=5+4x-x^2$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(c) From your graph, determine the value(s) of $x$ for which $x^{2}-4x-5=0$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Multiply $x^2-4x-5=0$ by $-1$: $5+4x-x^2=0$, i.e. $f(x)=0$.

So the solutions are the $x$-coordinates of the points where the curve cuts the $x$-axis ($y=0$): $x=-1$ and $x=5$.

(Check by factorising: $x^2-4x-5=(x-5)(x+1)=0$.)

**$x=-1$ or $x=5$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(d) Find the gradient of the curve at the point $(4,5)$, giving your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Draw the tangent to the curve at $(4,5)$ and measure its slope. The tangent passes through about $(3,9)$ and $(5,1)$:

gradient $=\dfrac{1-9}{5-3}=\dfrac{-8}{2}=-4$.

Check by differentiation: $f'(x)=4-2x$, so $f'(4)=4-8=-4$.

**Gradient $=-4.0$** (answers from the graph between about $-3.6$ and $-4.4$ are accepted).
